why.rationale: The CLI grades but does not narrate — every --help opens with an exit-code table the way a courthouse opens with case numbers. The exclusions all share one root: the surface speaks in verdicts before it speaks in verbs. My posture is to add a single 'narration band' above each existing block — a 2-3 line prose preface, a quickstart example, a state-orienting subcommand, an inline gloss for §-references, and a visible timeout warning. None of these rebuild the CLI; they soften the leading edge. Exit codes stay sovereign at the bottom where graders look. Operators arriving cold get a verb before a number. Density preserved, approachability added.
decisions_considered: Inline gloss vs hyperlink to PRD — chose gloss because terminal --help cannot click
Rewrite exit-code tables vs prepend narration — chose prepend to keep validator contracts intact
Add a new orient subcommand vs extend --help — chose subcommand (status/last-run) because state belongs in a verb
Auto-detect tmux/foreground vs warn on invocation — chose visible pre-flight warn line; auto-detect is invisible magic
Progressive disclosure via --verbose vs always-show short example — chose always-show one example
